88.09-11.additionalInfo: The points 88.09-11 Tong Shen/Wei/Bei are often needled together using the Dao Ma technique. They are known as the "Three Kidney-Penetrating Needles" [ _ = This group is located on the Kidney channel in Master Tung's acupuncture system. According to Master Tung's acupuncture, points on the thigh have a strong effect. They can regulate the whole body and treat diseases of the internal organs. The points 88.09-11 Tong Shen/Wei/Bei are important for treating kidney diseases. In the past, it was forbidden to use all six points simultaneously. Today, this prohibition has been lifted. Each of the three points can be used as an adjunct point in tonification treatments and also to prevent miscarriage. In cases of threatened miscarriage, the treatment should be performed for 15 consecutive days. This group of points is very similar to the "Three Lower Emperors" 77.17,19,21 Xia San Huang, which is also considered a primary group for kidney tonification. There are several ways to differentiate between them: Points on the thigh have a Yin within Yin nature, so the Three Kidney-Penetrating Needles are considered the most tonifying. Points in areas 55 and 66 have a Yang within Yin nature, so they treat excess. They can address excess Yang in the upper body. Points in area 77 are located in the transition between the two areas, so they have a Yang within Yin and Yin within Yin nature. They tonify but can also treat excess. The Three Kidney-penetrating Needles tonify and Constringe, whereas the Three Lower Emperors are more mobilizing. The Three Lower Emperors are contraindicated during pregnancy, while the Three Kidney-penetrating Needles can prevent miscarriage. The Three Lower Emperors are more often used for gynecological, genital, and neurological disorders, while the Three Kidney-Penetrating Needles are more for nephrological disorders and edema. The Three Lower Emperors are often combined with the Three Upper Emperors 88.12-14 Shang San Huang. For general tonification, 88.09-11 Tong Shen/Wei/Bei can be combined with 77.08, 09, 11 Si Hua. Both groups of points regulate the Spleen and Stomach, raise the clear and For general tonification, 88.09-11 Tong Shen/Wei/Bei can be combined with 77.08, 09, II Si Hua. Both groups of points regulate the Spleen and Stomach, raise the clear and lower the turbid, and tonify both postnatal and prenatal Qi. Among the three points: 88.09 Tong Shen is the primary point for treating dry mouth, sore throat, and Kidney deficiency. 88.10 Tong Wei is the primary point for treating stomach diseases. 88.11 Tong Bei is the primary point for treating shoulder and upper back disorders. Nephrolithiasis (kidney stones) While acupuncture does not physically crush kidney stones, it is a highly effective treatment for facilitating their natural passage, provided the stones are smaller than 6 millimeters. Rather than breaking the stone, the treatment focuses on creating the optimal physiological conditions for its expulsion. It works by relaxing and dilating the smooth muscle of the ureters (spasmolysis), allowing the stone to pass without getting stuck. Additionally, acupuncture promotes diuresis, creating a natural hydraulic pressure that helps flush the system, while simultaneously reducing the local inflammation and tissue swelling that can narrow the urinary tract. Ultimately, this approach significantly relieves the severe pain of renal colic and supports the smooth, natural exit of the stone. The character [ (Shen) in the name indicates the point's effect on the kidneys. The character [ ] (Wei) in the name suggests the point's effect on the stomach. Like the heart points, the names of these points represent a Taoist process of spiritual cultivation. Hidden within the kidneys is the Ming, our destiny, which we must discover. This discovery is achieved by looking into the Ming Men (Kidneys). To do this, we must control our desires, represented by the stomach — the things we hunger for. The spine represents the distribution of Original Qi to the Shu points on the Tai Yang channel of the leg, nourishing the organs with Original Qi. 88.12-14.additionalInfo: The points 88.12 Ming Huang, 88.13 Tian Huang, 88.14 Qi Huang are often needled together using the Dao Ma technique. This group of points is called the Upper Three Yellows, Shang San Huang [ ± E J. Some sources call this Dao Ma group the the Upper Three Emperors Shang San Huang [ ± E J. Upper Three Yellows are a primary group for influencing the liver, which governs the tendons and ligaments, stores blood, controls the wind, and ensures the smooth flow of Qi and blood. The Upper Three Emperors can support the kidneys. The liver's blood supports the kidney's essence. In this situation, the Upper Three Emperors are combined with the Lower Three Emperors. The Upper Three Yellows can also support the heart. The liver's blood nourishes the heart's Qi. In cases of heart deficiency, the Upper Three Emperors are combined with 88.01-03 Tong Guan/Shan/Tian. These points also have a primary innervation of the heart. The Upper Three Yellows can be used for emotional disorders related to liver Qi stagnation. The Upper Three Yellows can treat wind-related diseases. They can nourish the liver's blood and dispel wind. In conditions involving wind (tremors, Parkinson's disease, The Upper Three Yellows can treat wind-related diseases. They can nourish the liver's blood and dispel wind. In conditions involving wind (tremors, Parkinson's disease, Meniere's disease, dizziness, and vertigo), the Upper Three Emperors are combined with the Lower Three Emperors to allow the water (kidneys) to nourish the wood (liver). 88.17-19.additionalInfo: 88.17-19 Sima Zhong/Shang/Xia are often needled together using the Dao ma technique. When the three points are used together, they are called Sima, meaning "Four Horses." This is a primary group for strengthening the lungs and treating lung-related conditions such as asthma, pneumonia, and difficulty breathing. The lungs govern Qi, and this group of points can strengthen and regulate Qi. They can also regulate Wei Qi (defensive Qi). Due to the points' ability to regulate Qi, this group is frequently used. Sima has three main areas of influence: sensory organs, the chest, and the skin. When treating disorders located on one side of the body, such as facial paralysis, rib pain, or back pain, the points are needled on the opposite side. For other conditions, bilateral needling is used. Skin Disorders Sima is a primary group in Master Tung's acupuncture for treating skin diseases. When treating skin disorders, the points are needled bilaterally. The recommended needling technique is "Penetrating-Heaven Cooling" technique (Tou tian liang fu [iB J). In this technique, the needle is inserted into the deep level of the point, Qi is obtained, and a dispersing technique (lifting and thrusting) is performed. After ten minutes, Qi is obtained again, the needle is lifted to the middle level, and the dispersing technique is repeated. After another ten minutes, Qi is obtained again, the needle is lifted to the upper level, and the dispersing technique is performed again. The needle is left at this level until the end of the treatment. Hu Wen Zhi They are the primary points for treating "Qi" diseases. The Nei Jing (Inner Canon) states, "All diseases are born from Qi." If Qi is deficient, it lacks the strength to drive the blood, which inevitably causes "Blood Stasis". If Qi is replete (excessive), it will inevitably cause the blood to flow recklessly, resulting in stasis. Prolonged illness leads to Blood Stasis stemming from Qi stagnation. Therefore, the Si Ma points are effective for all Qi and Blood disease syndromes. Dr. Liao Li He adds further indications: exophthalmos (bulging eyes), dark spots on the face, nasal congestion, scleral redness, and gluttony (excessive eating). In ancient China, a carriage pulled by four horses was the ultimate symbol of speed and power. This image perfectly illustrates what these points do: they have a remarkable, rapid ability to regulate and strengthen the Qi in the body. And since in Chinese Medicine the Lungs govern the Qi, the connection here is absolutely perfect. The character "Xia" in the point's name indicates it is the lower point. The character "Zhong" in the point's name indicates it is the middle point. The character "Shang" in the point's name indicates it is the upper point.

88.20-22.additionalInfo: Often, 88.20 Xia Quan, 88.21 Zhong Quan, and 88.22 Shang Shang are combined using the Dao ma technique and then called the three springs 88.20-22 San Quan. The three springs are an essential combination for treating wind disorders in the upper part of the body, such as eyelid twitching, facial tics, and wind stroke. The innervation of these points indicates their effect on the facial nerve and their ability to treat facial paralysis. Since the lungs are responsible for defending against external wind invasion, these points also have innervation of the motor nerve of the lungs. The three springs are used to treat stroke involving the face and aphasia. They have less effect on the limbs (hemiplegia). When using the three springs to treat facial disorders, it is recommended to bleed the affected area and then needle the three springs on the opposite side. The middle and upper springs can be used to treat skin allergies. 88.25.additionalInfo: The point affects the brain, face, and limbs and can treat various disorders related to these areas, such as migraines, tinnitus, eye pain, limb weakness, hemiplegia, and numbness and pain in the upper limbs. The point also affects the spine and can treat conditions such as osteophytes in the spine, ankylosing spondylitis, and periostitis. The point can treat disorders caused by wind (in Chinese medicine), such as facial paralysis, dizziness, and hemiplegia (due to wind stroke). Wind can cause restlessness of the Shen, which is one of the reasons the point can treat itching, insomnia, and palpitations. This is a primary point that Master Tung used when treating Cambodian Prime Minister Lon Noll who suffered from a stroke and hemiplegia. 88.25 Zhong Jiu Li is a good point for treating pain when the source of the pain is unknown. It can be combined with 22.05 Ling Gu, 22.04 Da Bai, and Qi Li (88). Due to its ability to affect the nervous system, the point is used to treat insomnia and palpitations. 88.25 Zhong Jiu Li is often needled with Qi Li (88) in the Dao ma technique and 88.26-27 Shang/Xia Jiu Li. TongLing88.additionalInfo: The "Three Penetrators of the Leg," along with Tong Xin (88) and Tong Ling (88), treat heart diseases. Tong Xin (88) and Tong Ling (88) primarily address the mental aspect of the heart. Hu Wen Zhi These points do not appear in Master Tung's original text. Hu Wen Zhi introduced them. The five "Leg Penetrators" points are the most important for treating heart disease. They have an immediate effect on regulating blood circulation. Two out of the five points are typically selected. Penetrating Heaven Upper (Töng Tiän Shång Another point on the heart channel in the thigh is called Tong Tian Shang. It is located on the anterior middle line of the thigh (center of the patella), 13 cun superior to the upper border of the patella. This point is primarily used to treat shoulder disorders. Point Name Töng [iMI — to pass through, understand well, communicate, connect, open, clear. Ling — quick, alert, efficient, spirit, soul. The names of these points suggest their ability to address the heart's mental, emotional, and spiritual aspects. There are two groups of points with the character Tong (to open, communicate, penetrate). Both groups of points are associated with the spiritual aspects of the heart and kidneys, the Shen and Jing. The five points Tong Xin, Tong Ling, 88.01 Tong Guan, 88.02 Tong Shan, and 88.03 Tong Tian on the heart channel in the thigh represent a redemption. The journey begins at the lower points (Tong Xin and Tong Ling) and concludes at the upper point, 88.03 Tong Tian, where it connects with Heaven. Daoist process of spiritual The five points Tong Xin, Tong Ling, 88.01 Tong Guan, 88.02 Tong Shan, and 88.03 Tong Tian on the heart channel in the thigh represent a Daoist process of spiritual The heart represents consciousness, and at the first point, Tong Xin (penetrating the heart) opens the heart, allowing us to observe the Ling. The Ling, the Yin soul, resides in the blood and reflects the obstacles blocking and preventing spiritual redemption. In the third stage, the gate to the mysterious opens, Xuan Guan [ZICO]. Point 88.03 Tong Guan (penetrating the gate) symbolizes the gate's opening to the mystery. Unveiling the mystery allows us, at the fourth point, 88.02 Tong Shan (penetrate the mountain), to remove the barriers preventing spiritual redemption (the mountain symbolizes the obstacles blocking and preventing spiritual redemption). After removing these barriers, redemption occurs, and the Shen reconnects with Heaven. The final point, 88.03 Tong Tian (penetrate Heaven), symbolizes the reconnection with Heaven. To redeem the spirit, we need to be centered. When balanced at the center, we see reality as it is, without bias. Redemption passes through the center, and the heart channel runs through the center of the thigh.

TuLing.additionalInfo: This is a very important and effective point for treating Blood disorders. The point innervates the Spleen and Liver, the two organs in Chinese medicine that influence Blood. The Spleen governs Blood, and the Liver stores Blood. The point can treat anemia, but it also affects white blood cells. The points can be used in acute conditions where there is an increase in white blood cell count, such as viral, bacterial, or parasitic infections, as well as in allergic conditions. On the other hand, the point can also be used in conditions where the immune system is suppressed, manifesting as white blood cell deficiency (leukopenia). The point is very close to Tu Chang (88), which also affects Blood. To treat anemia, it can be needled together with 88 Tu Chang Yi and 88.10 Tong Wei in the horizontal Dao Ma technique.
